title: Projection pullbacks span first structure-sheaf cohomology of a product
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and let $X,Y$ be schemes over $\operatorname{Spec}(k)$ [def-weil-scheme-over-base] with proper structure morphisms [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Assume the structure ring homomorphisms $k\to\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$ and $k\to\Gamma(Y,\mathcal O_Y)$ are bijective. Let $P=X\times_k Y$ with projections $p_X,p_Y$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. For every $c\in H^1(P,\mathcal O_P)$, there exist $a\in H^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$ and $b\in H^1(Y,\mathcal O_Y)$ such that $p_X^*a+p_Y^*b=c$, where the cohomology and canonical pullback maps are those of [def-sc-structure-sheaf-cohomology-pullback]. No rational points or uniqueness of this expression are assumed or asserted.

source.place: Varieties, Lemma varieties-lemma-kunneth, Tag 0BED, applied in degree 1 to O_X and O_Y

proof.text: Properness over the affine scheme Spec k gives compactness of X and Y by proper_basic. The unit modules are quasi-coherent by the proved SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent_unit instance. Their relative diagonals are closed immersions by separatedness, hence affine. Apply picard_kunneth_qcoh in degree one and keep its formula on pure summand tensors.

Obtain the additive unit-coefficient comparisons eX,eY,eP, the degree-zero scalar coordinates dX,dY, and the two individual external-cup scalar formulas from the scalar comparison lemma. Compose eP with the Kunneth equivalence to get an additive surjection from the direct sum to the abelian H1 of the product.

For a degree-one summand index (p,q), p+q=1 implies (p,q)=(1,0) or (0,1). In the first case its pure tensor image is the X projection pullback of eX(dY(b) times a), with zero Y class; in the second it is the Y projection pullback of eY(dX(a) times b), with zero X class. The Kunneth generator formula identifies these with the direct-sum map values.

Prove that each direct-sum value is the sum of two projection pullbacks by DirectSum.induction_on, using TensorProduct.induction_on for each summand. Zero uses zero factor classes. The addition step adds factor classes separately; additivity of the three maps and the commutative-group rearrangement prove the required equality. Surjectivity of eP and of the Kunneth equivalence lifts any product class to a direct-sum element, and composing the equalities gives the assertion.
